author: Frank Asante Van Laarhoven

all_other_thresholds_passed.note: no candidate failed frames, distance, separation or windows

the_cross_scene_finding.statement: The binding constraint is the ROUTE GENERATOR, not the scene.
the_cross_scene_finding.mechanism: sample_episode_pair plans with A* and then string-pulls via smooth_path, which straightens a route wherever line of sight permits. In open interior floor space most start-goal pairs have line of sight, so the route is a straight line. In the Office example travelled distance and start-goal separation are equal to four decimal places (9.708 m), which is a straight line exactly.
the_cross_scene_finding.consequence: the predeclared long-horizon turn requirement (>= 3 changes of >= 30 degrees) and the frozen route generator are incompatible. Two scenes with different geometry, different occupancy bounds and different failure margins produce the same verdict for the same reason.
the_cross_scene_finding.prediction_for_warehouse: a third scene is expected to fail identically, because the generator rather than the scene is binding. Running Warehouse under this contract would spend Isaac time to re-derive a known result. Stated as a PREDICTION, not a result: no Warehouse candidate has been enumerated.

what_this_does_not_claim: not that Office cannot support long-horizon navigation
not that all possible Office routes fail
not that the frozen thresholds are wrong
not that the route generator is defective -- string-pulling is correct behaviour for a shortest-path planner; it is simply not a generator of turning routes

correct_next_step.but: a NEW preregistered collection experiment whose route population can produce turning routes -- multi-leg or waypoint routes -- with its generator, budget, seed and eligibility rules declared before any candidate is evaluated.
correct_next_step.must_not: overwrite or amend the Hospital or Office frozen results, or be presented as a repair to them. Both are valid measurements of the population they declared.
correct_next_step.thresholds: unchanged; this is a change of route population, not of the adequacy bar

non_claims: Office data, if ever collected, is a pipeline and loader proof and is never relabelled as Hospital data.

measurements_stand.why_they_stand: these record what the pipeline produced, and it did produce them

claim_downgraded.was: the binding constraint is the route generator: smooth_path string-pulls routes straight wherever line of sight permits
claim_downgraded.now: under a map that decoded 62% of its free space from unclassified cells, the generator produced predominantly straight routes. How much of that survives a corrected map is UNMEASURED.
claim_downgraded.reason: F-G5-1 resolved: build_occupancy decoded grid = (buf == OCCUPIED), so all 174,376 UNKNOWN cells (54% of Hospital's map) became free space. After inflation the planner's free space was 242,106 cells instead of 91,650. With 75% of the grid decoded as free, most of the scene looked like open space, and a shortest-path planner in open space produces straight lines whatever its smoothing does. String-pulling is real but is not established as the dominant cause.

PARTIAL_RETRACTION_20260909.hospital_g5_leg_strengthened: the 7 G5 failures are genuine -- those routes run into geometry that the map did not represent. NO_ADMISSIBLE_ROUTE is unaffected and its weaker leg is now its stronger one.
PARTIAL_RETRACTION_20260909.consequence_for_the_next_experiment: a turning-route population must not be designed against a cause that is not established. The corrected-map behaviour of the existing generator must be measured first.
PARTIAL_RETRACTION_20260909.residual_open_defect: gates/failures/F-G5-2.md -- cells explicitly marked UNOCCUPIED still carry solid geometry
